eyebrow: Moving the connection string into Key Vault
code:
az keyvault secret set --vault-name caldwell-kv \
  --name "OrderDbConnection" \
  --value "Server=caldwell-sql.database.windows.net;Database=Orders;..."

# App reads it at runtime via DefaultAzureCredential + SecretClient
# or an App Service Key Vault reference — never a literal in config
caption: The real connection string now lives in exactly one place, with an access policy and an audit log.

eyebrow: Why this beats a hardcoded string

steps.label: Not in source control
steps.sub: Nothing to leak through Git history, ever

steps.label: Not in a config file
steps.sub: Nothing for a CI/CD log or container image layer to capture

steps.label: Access is logged
steps.sub: Key Vault records every read, by which identity, and when

eyebrow: Rotation: a key vs. a secret
code:
# A key: Key Vault can rotate it automatically
az keyvault key rotation-policy update \
  --vault-name caldwell-kv --name caldwell-storage-cmk \
  --value rotation-policy.json

# A secret: Key Vault can only warn before it expires
az keyvault secret set-attributes --vault-name caldwell-kv \
  --name OrderDbConnection --expires 2027-01-15T00:00:00Z
caption: An Event Grid notification on near-expiry triggers a Function that actually rotates the DB credential.
